clue.text: Selling method wife used initially, in case

parts.note: 'old Dutch' is Cockney slang for a wife, so Dutch alone stands for wife

indicators.note: in puts that opening letter inside the word for a lawsuit

parts.note: a case in law is an action brought before a court

indicators.note: initially asks for only the opening letter of the word used

explanation.surface: A seller describes their method, noting that the wife's money went first on the case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' reads as a container for the wife, but it is a lawsuit. 'my old Dutch' is Cockney rhyming-era slang for one's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dutch auction is a sale where the price starts high and drops until a bidder accepts.

clue.text: Ship had picked up plants

indicators.note: picked up, in a down clue, lifts the pieces so they read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a sail is an old word for a ship, as in a fleet of twenty sail

explanation.surface: A vessel collected some greenery on its voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' turns SAIL + HAD, giving DAH + LIAS read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Dahlias are garden flowers grown from tubers, so they are plants.

clue.text: Cast delivering most of the words

indicators.note: most of means the short word the loses its final letter

parts.note: to have words is to argue, and an argument is a row

explanation.surface: An actor in a play delivers nearly all the lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like a theatre company, but it is the verb meaning to fling. 'most of' cuts THE to TH.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast a stone and to toss it are the same action, a synonym.

clue.text: Short-term loan records? How funny!

indicators.note: short tells us to cut the last letter off the name of that term

parts.note: Hilary is the law and university term running from January to Easter
IOUs are written notes acknowledging money borrowed

explanation.surface: Someone finds the paperwork for a brief loan unexpectedly amusing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short-term' reads as a phrase about the loan, but 'Short' trims HILARY, a British legal and academic term, to HILAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hilarious is extremely amusing, a stronger synonym.

clue.text: Part of skeleton concealed by artful natives

indicators.note: concealed by says the bone lies tucked away within the run of letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: Crafty locals hid a bone.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulna is one of the two forearm bones, so it is a piece of the skeleton.

clue.text: Transfer old volume into artist's keeping

indicators.note: keeping means the painter's name holds the two short pieces inside it

parts.note: J M W Turner is the English painter, a stock crossword artist

explanation.surface: An old book is handed over to a painter to look after.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn something over to someone is to hand it to them, a phrasal synonym.

clue.text: Scene of shooting attack

definitions.meaning: a film is shot ..., so being there is to be at the filming
an attack of illness is its ..., the beginning

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is the place where a film is shot; as one it is the start or assault.

clue.text: It secures admission for old man's amusement

parts.note: the old man is father, Pa, with the possessive giving PA'S
sport here means fun or amusement

explanation.surface: Dad's pastime gets him through the door.
explanation.definitionFit: A travel document gains its holder entry into a foreign country.

clue.text: Hairpiece found in London street

definitions.meaning: a single thread of hair is a piece of it
a major street running from Trafalgar Square to Fleet Street

explanation.definitionFit: A strand is one fibre of hair, and the Strand is a famous central London thoroughfare.

clue.text: Intransigent type found in vessel, on stern

indicators.note: on says the ship comes alongside the word for severe, here following it

parts.note: stern means severe or hard
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: An unbending character turns up aboard a ship, at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stern' looks like the rear of the vessel, but it is the adjective meaning severe.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone uncompromising who refuses to move from a fixed position is a hardliner.

clue.text: Jump off

definitions.meaning: to jump in surprise is to give a ...
the off is the beginning of a race

explanation.definitionFit: A sudden jerk of surprise and the beginning of a race share this word.

clue.text: Heading for, centre where some cases are treated

definitions.meaning: medical cases are treated when admitted to a hospital ward, so being in a ward

explanation.definitionFit: Inward motion goes towards the middle; split in two it says patients are in a hospital ward.

clue.text: Gas main

parts.note: not a pipe but a body of water, main being an old word for the sea, that supplies Britain with natural gas

explanation.definitionFit: The North Sea is the main, or sea, from which British natural gas is drilled.

clue.text: Article removed from manse or other-address of churchman

indicators.note: other suggests a different arrangement of the remaining letters
removed from says the article is taken out of the vicarage word

parts.note: A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A notice about something taken out of the vicarage or another vicar's home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed from' takes A out of MANSE, leaving MNSE; 'other' rearranges MNSE + OR.
explanation.definitionFit: A sermon is a speech delivered from the pulpit, address meaning a formal talk.

clue.text: Interpret only to make new changes

parts.note: to read a situation is to interpret it
just means only, as in just one

explanation.surface: Translating something merely to bring in fresh alterations.
explanation.definitionFit: To readjust is to alter something again, adapting it afresh.

clue.text: Blue joining one club after another, say

indicators.note: say means the joined club names only sound like the word wanted, not spelt the same

parts.note: a wedge and a wood are both golf clubs, so the second follows the first

explanation.surface: A sad golfer moves from one club to the next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' looks like a mood; it is the pale blue of Wedgwood pottery. The spelling drops the E of wedge.
explanation.definitionFit: Wedgwood blue is the pale shade used on the famous English jasperware pottery.

clue.text: Metal moulded initially in plant

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the flower's name

parts.note: a geranium is a flowering garden plant

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of moulded

explanation.surface: Some metal is shaped, starting inside a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory beside 'moulded', but it is the flower GERANIUM, with M inserted.
explanation.definitionFit: Germanium is a grey metalloid element used in semiconductors.

clue.text: Bitter criticism in dreadful tirade about one book

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the following pieces
dreadful suggests the letters of tirade are mangled

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A harsh attack appears in an awful rant about a single volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' rearranges TIRADE into DIATRE, and 'about' wraps it round IB.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a forceful verbal attack, a near synonym of tirade itself.

clue.text: Produces family members in army uniform, partly

parts.note: a tree bears fruit, that is produces it
kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: Relatives are produced wearing part of a soldier's dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A bearskin is the tall fur cap worn by Guards regiments, one piece of their ceremonial dress.

clue.text: Animated deer endlessly circles in the grass

indicators.note: endlessly means the name loses its last letter

parts.note: Bambi is the deer of the Disney cartoon
circles look like the letter O, so two of them give OO

explanation.surface: A cartoon fawn is running round and round in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims BAMBI to BAMB, and 'circles' supplies two O shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Bamboo is a giant woody member of the grass family.

clue.text: Titillating collection of books man conceals

indicators.note: conceals means the name holds the testament abbreviation inside it

parts.note: Eric is a man's name
OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A man hides a stash of racy books.
explanation.definitionFit: Something erotic arouses sexual interest, which is what titillating means.

clue.text: Scoundrel put on charge for something shocking

indicators.note: put on, in a down clue, means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible man
rent is a charge paid for property

explanation.surface: A rogue is billed for something outrageous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shocking' suggests scandal, but the definition is electric current, which can shock.
explanation.definitionFit: An electric current gives a jolt to anyone who touches a live wire.

clue.text: Bill needs this army rank

definitions.meaning: a parliamentary bill must win most votes to pass
the rank held by a major in the army

explanation.definitionFit: Winning more than half the votes passes a bill; the same word names the office of a major.

clue.text: Part of flight for one coming out of retirement

definitions.meaning: the vertical piece of a step in a flight of stairs
someone getting up after retiring to bed, an early or late getter-up

explanation.definitionFit: The upright of a stair and a person getting up from bed share the word.

clue.text: Old fellow right to go after faux pas

indicators.note: to go after puts the abbreviation behind the word for a blunder

parts.note: a gaffe is a social blunder

explanation.surface: An elderly man makes a social blunder and is put right afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaffer is a British colloquial term for an elderly man.

clue.text: Brother and father holding song up

indicators.note: holding means the priest's abbreviation contains the reversed song

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, reads the song from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an air is a simple tune or song

explanation.surface: A monk and a priest are holding up a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brother' is the definition, not part of a family list with 'father'; in a down clue 'up' means read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A friar is a member of a religious order, addressed as Brother.

clue.text: Raised pet duck for food

indicators.note: raised, in a down clue, means the pet word is read upwards

parts.note: a cat is a household pet
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, written like O

explanation.surface: A pet is reared alongside a duck for food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' turns CAT into TAC. A cricket duck is a batsman's score of nought.
explanation.definitionFit: A taco is a Mexican folded tortilla with a filling, a kind of food.

clue.text: Pacific areas where you'll find sea so stormy

indicators.note: stormy tells us the letters of the following words are tossed about

explanation.surface: Regions of the Pacific where rough waters meet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pacific' is not the ocean but the adjective meaning peaceful, and 'sea' is fodder, not scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: Oases are fertile spots of calm in a desert, places of peace.

clue.text: It is held by book's heroine to give special slant to character

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: held by means the following short word is gripped inside the heroine's name

parts.note: Alice is the heroine of Lewis Carroll's Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: A fictional heroine takes on something that gives a typeface its lean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' means a printed letter, not a person in the book, so the definition is about typography.
explanation.definitionFit: Italicising a letter sets it in a sloping typeface, which slants it.

clue.text: Remit, possibly, an award

parts.note: the wordplay order of plus the word merit would yield remit

explanation.surface: A remittance may be a kind of prize.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards as a clue: an order (rearrangement) of MERIT gives REMIT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Order of Merit is a British honour awarded by the monarch.
